title: Map every CONVERT* and PROMOTE* table dependency and side effect
acceptance: Every procedure has documented local reads and updates, Aderant test/production reads and writes, key-allocation calls, and dynamic SQL.
The load-order graph and cycles are documented and checked against the current procedure bodies.
Uncertain, obsolete, and environment-specific behavior is listed as an explicit decision rather than silently retained.

title: Define and version the eleven-table staging compatibility contract
acceptance: NAMES, CLIENTS, ADDRESSES, CONTACTS, MATTERS, BILLGROUPS, ASSIGNMENTS, NOTES, RATES, VENDORS, and VENDORADDRESSES have a versioned data dictionary.
Every column has type, nullability, semantics, sensitivity, source/target role, and retirement status.
Compatibility tests prove current procedures can consume the contract or compatibility views without change.

title: [Epic] Build end-to-end audit and governed data changes
acceptance: Every application-mediated update to landing, staging, Aderant test, or Aderant production is executed as a versioned governed change set.
Executions retain actor, reason, scope, approval, before/after evidence, lineage, transaction result, verification, and reversal history.
Temporary rehearsal and go-live corrections expire predictably without deleting their audit history.
Direct database writes are restricted and native database audit events without a matching MergerManager execution are reported.

title: Define the immutable audit-event and change-set contracts
acceptance: The ChangeSet contract defines identity/version, reason, phase, environment, scope, mutation hash, preconditions, evidence policy, verification, recovery, activation, and governance.
Append-only audit events cover drafting, validation, approval, execution, commit/failure, verification, retirement, reversal, supersession, and evidence deletion.
Identifiers and correlation rules link project revision, run, pipeline step, change definition, execution, row evidence, approval, and native database event.
Canonical serialization and hash-chain rules have golden compatibility tests.

title: Implement the audited data-mutation gateway
acceptance: UI, pipeline, typed rules, and imported SQL use one gateway for all landing, staging, Aderant test, and Aderant production writes.
The gateway enforces project/run/environment identity, authorization, phase eligibility, idempotency, timeout, transaction policy, row bounds, and approved content hash.
Architecture tests fail when other application infrastructure requests a write-capable database path.
Commit, rollback, partial-failure, retry, and cancellation behavior is deterministic and auditable.

title: Capture row-level before/after evidence and lineage
acceptance: Every affected row records stable business key, entity/table, before/after diff, lineage, execution identity, transaction outcome, and verification linkage.
Large row images use encrypted chunked evidence artifacts with queryable indexes, offsets, classifications, and cryptographic hashes.
Sensitive fields are masked in normal UI and logs while specifically authorized audit workflows can retrieve retained evidence.
Retention deletion leaves an auditable tombstone and preserves hash-chain explainability.

title: Implement phase-bound temporary changes for rehearsal and go-live
acceptance: Change sets can target PreExtract, PostLanding, PostNormalize, Pre/PostTestConvert, PreProductionPromote, and PostGoLive phases.
Eligibility is restricted by exact project, environment, run or bounded run range, lifecycle phase, activation window, and dependency changes.
One-shot changes retire after verified execution; recurring changes require a bounded window and are reevaluated for every run.
Closure is blocked while an expired, unverified, or unexpectedly active temporary production change remains.

title: Implement preview, approval, verification, and reversal workflows
acceptance: Preview shows environment, phase, selected row bounds, redacted before/proposed-after samples, impacted relationships, validation effects, hashes, and recovery warnings.
Approval binds to the exact project, mutation, parameters, selector result, environment, and precondition hash and expires when any input changes.
Separation of duties and a time-bounded break-glass workflow are enforceable by environment policy.
Verification and reversal are governed executions; reversal never erases or edits the original history.

title: Build the audit explorer and evidence export
acceptance: Operators can trace a business row across source lineage, landing, staging, test conversion, production promotion, corrections, verification, and reversal.
Search filters include project/run, phase, environment, entity/key, change set, actor, approval, time, result, and active/expired status.
Go-live evidence export includes all applied, failed, reversed, superseded, and active changes plus unmatched native database events.
Exports apply authorization, masking, encryption, retention classification, and tamper-evident hashes.

title: Enforce least-privilege writes and reconcile native database audit
acceptance: Ordinary source and operator profiles are read-only; environment-specific gateway identities receive only reviewed mutation operations.
Database-native auditing captures direct DML, DDL, permission changes, identity, time, target, and break-glass activity according to platform capability.
A reconciliation process correlates native events to gateway executions and raises blocking findings for unmatched writes.
Break-glass access is time-bound, separately authorized, monitored, and requires retrospective evidence and approval.

title: Define merger run lifecycle, checkpoints, and provenance
acceptance: States and allowed transitions exist for discovery, full rehearsal, delta, cutover, retry, failure, cancellation, and closure.
Project, run, step, row provenance, checkpoint, artifact, approval, exception, and governed-change references are defined.
Existing COMPANY_CODE, BATCH, PROMOTE, and test/production identifier behavior has an explicit compatibility mapping.
Checkpoint and resume rules cannot bypass audit, validation, approval, or environment gates.

title: Select the active client conversion procedure and validate Aderant safety constraints
acceptance: CONVERTCLIENTS, CONVERTCLIENTS_OG, and CONVERTCLIENTSHOLDER are diffed by behavior and target side effects.
One supported path is selected or a consolidation plan is approved; obsolete variants are clearly marked.
Required permissions, transaction boundaries, backup/restore expectations, and prohibited production operations are documented.

title: Record security, privacy, and data-retention requirements
acceptance: Data classifications and least-privilege roles are defined for source, staging, Aderant test, and production.
Credential storage, log redaction, encryption, evidence export, retention, and secure deletion requirements are approved.
The threat model covers malicious source values, SQL injection, unsafe dynamic SQL, and accidental production execution.

title: Scaffold the .NET MAUI solution and automated test projects
acceptance: The supported .NET/MAUI baseline and desktop platforms are recorded.
App, Domain, Application, Infrastructure, connector, Aderant target, and test project boundaries compile.
Dependency injection, configuration validation, structured logging, navigation, and a first automated test run locally and in CI.

title: [Epic] Build the multi-project workspace and portable merger project system
acceptance: One portable .mergerproj manifest authoritatively captures each merger's scope, decisions, ETL rules, policies, versions, and non-secret references.
Several projects can remain open and run concurrently without shared mutable current-project state or cross-project resource disposal.
Every run records an immutable, content-hashed project snapshot and referenced-artifact hashes.

title: Define the .mergerproj schema and canonical serialization
acceptance: A published JSON Schema defines identity, versions, connection-profile references, scope, decisions, mappings, transformations, validations, crosswalks, and pipeline policy.
Canonical UTF-8 serialization is deterministic and excludes credentials, extracted data, mutable run state, and machine-specific absolute paths.
Relative artifact references are constrained beneath the project root and can carry SHA-256 content hashes.
Golden files cover minimal, complete, invalid, unknown-field, and unsupported-version manifests.

title: Implement atomic project persistence, migration, and recovery
acceptance: Create, open, save, save-as, and close validate the manifest and preserve its stable ProjectId.
Saves use temporary-file flush and atomic replacement with a recoverable backup and never leave a partially written manifest.
Supported older versions migrate through explicit tested transformations; unsupported major versions open read-only or fail clearly.
External edits and concurrent writers are detected using content hashes and a per-project write lease.

title: Implement concurrent project sessions and resource isolation
acceptance: Every open project owns a ProjectSession, dependency-injection scope, cancellation boundary, working directory, log context, and run coordinator.
Commands and background notifications carry project/session identity; there is no process-wide mutable current project.
Closing or failing one project does not cancel, dispose, alter, or misroute activity for another project.
Concurrency tests run at least two projects with different profiles and overlapping pipeline stages.

title: Implement secure connection-profile and secret references
acceptance: Project manifests store connector type and stable profile identity but no password, token, secret-bearing connection string, or encryption key.
Profiles resolve through an approved secure store and distinguish source, staging, Aderant test, and Aderant production environments.
Missing, unauthorized, or environment-mismatched profiles fail before pipeline execution and produce redacted diagnostics.
Exporting or cloning a project never transfers secrets.

title: Snapshot decisions and ETL rules for reproducible runs
acceptance: Starting a run validates and canonically serializes the saved project and hashes every execution-affecting referenced artifact.
The immutable snapshot records decisions, mappings, transformations, validations, crosswalk references, pipeline policy, and contract versions.
Editing the project after a run starts does not change that run; a subsequent run receives a new revision and hash.
Checkpoints and reconciliation evidence include the project snapshot hash.

title: Build the MAUI project explorer and multi-project navigation
acceptance: Operators can create, open, switch, save, close, and reopen multiple projects from a project explorer.
Each project clearly displays identity, dirty/read-only state, environment, active runs, blocking findings, and save conflicts.
Recent/open project paths and UI state are app-local and cannot alter merger behavior.
Navigation and progress remain associated with the correct project under concurrent background activity.

title: [Epic] Build reusable source-system templates
acceptance: A new merger project can inherit a certified template for a compatible source PMS and staging-contract version, then record only explicit firm-specific decisions and overrides.
Compatibility uses source product/version metadata plus schema fingerprint and drift analysis rather than vendor name or column-name similarity alone.
Runs snapshot the resolved template rules and project overlay with complete provenance.
Templates contain no prior source-firm data, credentials, environment identifiers, allocated Expert IDs, approvals, or firm-specific crosswalk values.

title: Define the source-system template contract and certification model
acceptance: The versioned contract covers identity, PMS/DBMS compatibility, schema fingerprint, extraction, mappings, transformations, validations, generic crosswalks, required decisions, limitations, and synthetic tests.
Draft, Candidate, Certified, Deprecated, and Withdrawn states have explicit permissions and transition requirements.
Templates exclude firm identity/data, credentials, absolute paths, environment IDs, run history, approvals, allocated Expert IDs, and firm-specific crosswalk values.
Canonical packaging, signing/hashing, semantic versioning, and staging-contract compatibility have golden tests.

title: Create a merger project from a compatible template and overlay
acceptance: Project creation selects an exact template version only after displaying compatibility, limitations, required decisions, and schema drift.
Inherited, parameterized, overridden, disabled, and newly created rules retain template/project provenance and rationale.
Firm-specific identities, crosswalks, credentials, environments, and approvals start empty and cannot leak from template fixtures.
Runs store the fully resolved rule set, template identity/version, project overlay, fingerprint, and compatibility report.

title: Generate source schema fingerprints and template drift reports
acceptance: Fingerprints cover required/optional objects, columns, types, nullability, keys, relationships, cardinality assumptions, and connector capabilities.
Drift classifies exact matches, compatible variations, missing elements, unexpected elements, changed relationships, customization collisions, and uncertified product/platform versions.
Safe matches may be accepted by policy; uncertain differences become explicit project decisions and unresolved coverage findings.
No source field is silently ignored or matched only because its name resembles a template field.

title: Promote sanitized project rules into a new template version
acceptance: Operators explicitly select candidate extraction, mapping, transformation, validation, and decision assets from a successful project.
Promotion removes or parameterizes firm-specific values and scans for confidential data, credentials, server/environment references, absolute paths, and allocated IDs.
Real data examples are replaced by synthetic fixtures and known limitations and compatibility changes are documented.
Publication creates a new immutable version after tests, independent review, and approval; it never mutates the prior template.

title: Implement template upgrades and three-way overlay reconciliation
acceptance: Upgrade compares the old template, new template, and project overlay without changing an active run snapshot.
Unchanged inherited rules advance automatically while conflicting overrides, removals, and contract changes require explicit resolution.
The operator sees mapping, validation, decision, limitation, fixture, and staging-contract impacts before saving.
A failed or canceled upgrade leaves the project on its original template version and remains recoverable.

title: Build a certified template catalog and compatibility test suite
acceptance: The catalog resolves immutable versions, certification state, owners, compatibility range, staging contract, limitations, release notes, and withdrawal advisories.
Every candidate/certified template runs synthetic source fixtures through extraction and mapping to deterministic validated staging output.
Catalog policy prevents withdrawn templates and clearly warns for candidate/deprecated templates when creating or upgrading a project.
Historical run evidence can resolve template metadata even after a version is deprecated or withdrawn.

title: Define source connector contracts and capability model
acceptance: Contracts cover connection tests, metadata discovery, typed reads, paging/streaming, cancellation, and safe sampling.
Capabilities express vendor differences without leaking vendor APIs into application or UI layers.
A connector contract-test suite can be reused by every future DBMS adapter.

title: Implement the SQL Server reference source connector
acceptance: A least-privilege SQL Server profile connects, validates capabilities, and streams typed rows with cancellation.
Queries use parameterization and safely quoted identifiers; credentials and source values are redacted from logs.
The connector passes the shared contract tests against a disposable database.

title: Implement source schema discovery and profiling
acceptance: Discovery records schemas, tables/views, columns, types, nullability, keys, relationships, and row-count estimates.
Profiling reports null, distinct, length/range, parseability, and duplicate-key signals with bounded sampling.
Operators can export a reproducible discovery snapshot without exporting confidential sample values by default.

title: Provision run-aware landing, staging, crosswalk, and quality schemas
acceptance: Idempotent migrations provision control, landing, the eleven-table staging contract, crosswalk, and quality storage.
Rows can be traced to source system/object/key, extraction, transformation version, and run.
Upgrade and compatibility tests cover an existing conversion database without deleting legacy objects.

title: Build the mapping and transformation rule engine
acceptance: Rules support direct mappings, constants, conversions, defaults, lookups, composition, and conditional logic.
Rules are versioned, deterministic, testable, and previewable against bounded source samples.
Coverage identifies every required staging column as mapped, defaulted, derived, or unresolved.

title: Build crosswalk management with import, export, and validation
acceptance: Operators can edit and bulk import/export versioned source-to-canonical code and identifier mappings.
Duplicate, missing, conflicting, and unused mappings are surfaced before a run.
Every change records author, time, reason, and affected runs without placing confidential values in logs.

title: Implement dependency-aware pipeline orchestration and checkpoints
acceptance: The pipeline plans extraction, normalization, validation, test conversion, and production promotion from a dependency graph.
Steps expose progress, cancellation, duration, row counts, checkpoints, and structured failure details.
Interrupted runs resume only from safe checkpoints and cannot skip required validation or approval gates.

title: Implement validation findings, exception approvals, and gating
acceptance: Rules cover schema, required values, types, referential integrity, uniqueness, crosswalk completeness, and domain constraints.
Findings have severity, stable identity, source/stage provenance, owner, status, and remediation evidence.
Blocking findings prevent target execution; exceptions require recorded scope, reason, approver, and expiry.

title: Implement reconciliation reports and evidence export
acceptance: Reports compare source, landing, staging, Aderant test, and production counts and control totals by entity and disposition.
Missing, duplicate, rejected, and changed records drill down to provenance without exposing secrets.
An immutable evidence package records versions, timings, checks, exceptions, and approvals for sign-off.

title: Implement the deterministic staging-to-Expert loader with plan and dry-run modes
acceptance: A versioned product-owned loader profile fixes the target tables, columns, procedures, and dependency graph for a declared staging-contract and Expert compatibility pair.
Merger projects can select a compatible loader and bounded parameters but cannot edit target mappings, loader SQL, or dependency order.
The adapter verifies target-firm environment identity, permissions, contract/profile versions, prerequisites, validation status, approvals, and expected row bounds.
Plan/dry-run displays the resolved fixed graph and intended effects without changing Expert or allocating keys; test conversion and production promotion use distinct audited permissions.

title: Migrate contacts, clients, and addresses end to end
acceptance: NAMES, CLIENTS, ADDRESSES, and CONTACTS mappings run through landing, staging, validation, test conversion, and reconciliation.
Shared names, contact relationships, address selection, and test/production identifier updates have deterministic fixtures.
The production path remains gated and is proven with an approved non-production target or safe harness.

title: Migrate matters, bill groups, and assignments end to end
acceptance: MATTERS, BILLGROUPS, and ASSIGNMENTS run through the complete pipeline in verified dependency order.
Client/matter codes, responsible and billing personnel, percentages, effective dates, and bill-group relationships are validated.
Fixtures cover missing references, duplicate codes, closed matters, split assignments, and rejected rows.

title: Migrate rates, vendors, vendor addresses, and notes end to end
acceptance: RATES, VENDORS, VENDORADDRESSES, and NOTES run through the complete pipeline and reconciliation.
Rate scope/effective dates, vendor tax-sensitive data, address linkage, and client/matter note ownership are validated and redacted appropriately.
Fixtures cover boundary dates, overlapping rates, missing parents, duplicate vendors, and long note text.

title: Support idempotent rehearsal, delta, retry, and cutover runs
acceptance: Full and delta eligibility is explicit per entity and no longer relies on cloned _DELTA tables.
Retries after key allocation or partial writes are safe, detect prior effects, and do not create duplicates.
Cutover records freeze points, approvals, run versions, recovery steps, and final evidence.

title: Build the MAUI mapping, preview, validation, and run experience
acceptance: Operators can move from project overview through discovery, mapping, preview, findings, plan, run progress, and reconciliation.
Long work remains responsive, cancellable, resumable, and accessible; closing or navigating the UI does not corrupt a run.
Production-impacting actions clearly identify environment, scope, blocking findings, and required approval.

title: Create deterministic fixtures and connector contract tests
acceptance: A small synthetic merger dataset covers all eleven staging tables without real client data.
Golden outputs cover mapping, validation, ordering, retries, reconciliation, and procedure compatibility.
Every connector runs the same capability and behavior suite in a disposable environment.

title: Add CI, packaging, diagnostics, and support matrix
acceptance: CI restores, builds, tests, scans, and publishes diagnostics without secrets or confidential fixture data.
Signed/versioned desktop packages and upgrade behavior exist for approved platforms.
The support matrix lists OS, .NET/MAUI, DBMS/driver, SQL Server, and Aderant versions with tested status.

title: Publish the reusable merger playbook and automation coverage matrix
acceptance: The playbook covers initiation, discovery, mapping, configuration, rehearsal, remediation, cutover, verification, and closure.
Each WBS task identifies owner, inputs, outputs, entry/exit criteria, tool automation, and required human decision.
A completed merger can promote reusable mappings/rules without carrying its source data, credentials, or company-specific objects forward.
